newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says crucial monsoon delayed.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says crucial monsoon delayed.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Meterology Department said on Wednesday that the crucial southwest monsoon showers had been delayed, but electricity officials said it would not affect the power situation in the Indian Ocean island.
"Conditions (for the monsoon) are weak. We're not expecting it to come even in one week's time," a department official told Reuters.
Officials of the state utility Ceylon Electricity Board said hydropower reservoirs had 442 gigawatt hours, or 35 percent of storage capacity, as of Wednesday.
"We do expect the monsoons to break soon and bring enough water into the reservoirs," one official said.
"But even if we get only marginal rains, with the new plants coming on stream, we should be able to manage."

Sri Lanka relies heavily on rains to fill its hydropower reservoirs, which currently meet 85 percent of the country's power needs. It is building several diesel- and gas-fired power plants to reduce its dependency on hydro power.
A severe drought last year led to long power cuts and affected economic growth.
